provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: My identity
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state their names.
The pupils should be able to list two talents they have.

Introduction:
We are all special. God made each one of us different.

Content:
Identity means who you are. You have a name. You have talents. Talent is something you can do well. Some children can sing well. Some can draw well. Some can run fast. You are special because you are you.

Class activity:
Stand up and say your name. Then show one talent you have.

Evaluation questions:
What is your name? What is one talent you have? Why are you special?

Summary:
God made you special with unique talents.

topics.title: Integrity jar
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what honesty is.
The pupils should be able to identify honest actions.

Introduction:
Last week we learned we are special. Today we learn about being honest.

Content:
Integrity means being honest. Honesty is telling the truth. It is doing the right thing even when no one is watching. When you are honest, you put a marble in our class integrity jar.

Class activity:
When you do something honest this week, tell the class and put a marble in the jar.

Evaluation questions:
What is honesty? Give an example of honest action. What do we do with marbles?

Summary:
We fill our integrity jar with honest acts.

topics.title: Respect relay
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate respect at home.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate respect at school.

Introduction:
We have learned about honesty. Today we learn about respect.

Content:
Respect means being kind to others. We show respect at home to parents and siblings. We show respect at school to teachers and friends. We show respect in worship places to elders and leaders.

Class activity:
We will play a respect relay. Act out showing respect at home, then at school, then in worship.

Evaluation questions:
How do you show respect at home? How do you show respect at school? Where else do we show respect?

Summary:
We show respect everywhere we go.

topics.title: Work ethics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain the meaning of doing their best.
The pupils should be able to identify tasks that need finishing.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about respect. Today we learn about working hard.

Content:
Work ethics means how we work. We should do our best. Not the least. We should finish what we start. Like when you clean your desk, clean it well. When you draw a picture, finish it strong.

Class activity:
Each child will start a simple task. Like building a tower with blocks. Finish your tower strong.

Evaluation questions:
What does do your best mean? Should we stop before finishing? What happens when we finish strong?

Summary:
We do our best and finish what we start.

topics.title: Money and me
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what saving means.
The pupils should be able to list wise choices with money.

Introduction:\Today we learn about money. Money is like naira coins.

Content:
Money is what we buy things with. We can save money. Saving means keeping money for later. We can give money to help others. We make wise choices with money. Like buying food instead of too toffees.

Class activity:
Each child will get play naira. Choose to save some or give some.

Evaluation questions:
What is saving? What is one wise choice with money? Should we spend all our money?

Summary:
We save, give and make wise choices with money.

topics.title: Media discernment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify good things to watch.
The pupils should be able to explain what builds them up.

Introduction:
We have learned about money. Today we learn about what we watch on TV.

Content:
Media is what we watch and listen to. We choose what builds us up. Builds us means makes us good and strong. Some shows teach us kindness. Some shows make us want to shout. We talk about what we watch with parents.

Class activity:
We will draw a picture of something good we watched on TV.

Evaluation questions:
What is media? What builds you up? Should we talk about what we watch?

Summary:
We choose good things to watch and talk about them.

topics.title: Kindness counts
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what kindness is.
The pupils should be able to perform an act of kindness.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about choosing good things to watch. Today we learn about kindness.

Content:
Kindness means being good to others. Like sharing your toys. Like helping a friend who falls. We have a kindness tree in class. When you are kind, you add a leaf to the tree.

Class activity:
Each child will do one kind thing for another child. Then add a leaf to our kindness tree.

Evaluation questions:
What is kindness? Give an example of kindness. What do we add to our kindness tree?

Summary:
We fill our kindness tree with kind acts.

topics.title: Perseverance
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain perseverance.
The pupils should be able to tell a story about not giving up.

Introduction:
We have learned about kindness. Today we learn about not giving up.

Content:
Perseverance means try, try, try again. Like when you learn to write your name and it is hard. You keep trying until you get it right. There is a story about a child who wanted to learn to ride a bike. Fell many times but kept trying.

Class activity:
We will try to build the tallest tower with blocks. If it falls, we try again.

Evaluation questions:
What is perseverance? What happens when we try and try again? Tell about something hard you did not give up on.

Summary:
We keep trying even when things are hard.

topics.title: Team spirit
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what team spirit is.
The pupils should be able to work in a group to complete a task.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about perseverance. Today we learn about working together.

Content:
Team spirit means together we win. Like when we play football together. If we all pass the ball, we can score. If one person keeps the ball, we may not win. We do group challenges like cleaning the classroom together.

Class activity:
We will work in small groups to build a puzzle. Work together to finish.

Evaluation questions:
What is team spirit? Why is it good to work together? What is one group challenge we can do?

Summary:
Together we can do more than alone.

topics.title: Revision and character crown
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall character traits learned.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate good character.

Introduction:
This week we revise all we learned this term. We also get character crowns.

Content:
We have learned about being special, honest, respectful, hardworking, moneywise, media smart, kind, persevering, and team players. Today we review these. Then we have a crown ceremony. Each child gets a crown for good character.

Class activity:
Each child will tell one thing they learned this term. Then we will have our crown ceremony.

Evaluation questions:
What is one thing you learned this term? Why do we get crowns? What is good character?

Summary:
We celebrate our good character with crowns.
